ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ AD$ bisects $ \angle BAC$ and intersects $ BC$ at point $ D$, $ DE \perp AB$ with the foot of the perpendicular being $ E$. If $ DE=1$ and $ AC=4$, then what is the area of $ \triangle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $DF \perp AC$ at $F$, as shown in the figure,\\
since $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $DE\perp AB$, $DF\perp AC$,\\
therefore $DF=DE=1$,\\
therefore the area of $\triangle ADC = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 1 = \boxed{2}$.
